actions.justification: Mandatory first step — assess HR, BP, SpO2, RR for hemodynamic stability in this STEMI patient. Required per AHA guidelines as immediate priority.
AHA Class I recommendation: 12-lead ECG must be obtained and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact to confirm STEMI and guide emergent reperfusion strategy.
Mandatory clinical history to characterize onset, duration, and character of chest pain for risk stratification and to guide treatment decisions.
MANDATORY: Immediate cath lab activation is required for STEMI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes. Patient has STEMI with three-vessel disease requiring urgent reperfusion.
MANDATORY: Aspirin 325mg chewable is a Class I recommendation for all STEMI patients as part of dual antiplatelet therapy to reduce platelet aggregation and improve outcomes.

MANDATORY: P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or clopidogrel) is required as part of dual antiplatelet therapy for STEMI per AHA guidelines. Note: prasugrel is relatively contraindicated in patients requiring CABG; clopidogrel preferred given three-vessel disease and anticipated CABG.
MANDATORY action - Heparin or enoxaparin is required as adjunctive anticoagulation therapy for STEMI per AHA guidelines. This is the only remaining mandatory action and must be completed immediately.
Primary PCI must be arranged to meet door-to-balloon time target of <90 minutes. Patient is at 30 minutes since arrival; this is time-critical per AHA Class I guidelines.
IV access is essential for administration of anticoagulation, medications, and any emergency drugs. Should be established immediately to facilitate ongoing treatment.

Troponin measurement is essential to establish baseline infarct size, confirm myocardial injury extent, and monitor for post-PCI reperfusion. Serial troponins will guide further management and CABG timing.

Formal ECG interpretation is needed to assess ST resolution post-PCI, confirm reperfusion success, and evaluate for any new conduction abnormalities or ongoing ischemia in the setting of three-vessel disease.
Three-vessel CAD with diabetes requires urgent cardiology/cardiac surgery consultation for CABG planning. This is a Class I indication for surgical revascularization in this clinical context.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 78, BP 125/75, SpO2 98%) with no signs of acute heart failure or cardiogenic shock. Beta-blocker therapy is indicated per AHA guidelines as adjunctive therapy in STEMI to reduce myocardial oxygen demand and risk of arrhythmia.

Patient has three-vessel CAD post-STEMI. Right-sided ECG (V4R) is important to evaluate for right ventricular involvement, which would contraindicate nitrates and alter fluid management. This is a safety-critical assessment.

Obtaining prior ECG for comparison is clinically useful in a patient with known three-vessel CAD and diabetes to assess baseline ST changes and differentiate new from chronic ECG findings, aiding surgical planning for CABG.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (BP 125/75, MAP 92) and right-sided ECG has already been obtained to rule out RV infarction. Nitrates are appropriate for ongoing ischemic symptoms in this stable STEMI patient without contraindications.
Morphine may be considered for ongoing chest pain/discomfort not relieved by nitrates in STEMI patients. Assess pain level and administer if patient reports significant discomfort.

Although SpO2 is 98% and supplemental oxygen is not routinely indicated in normoxic STEMI patients, this action confirms oxygen status and ensures readiness if saturation drops post-PCI. It is the most clinically relevant optional action available given all mandatory actions are already completed.

Patient has three-vessel CAD and is post-PCI with stable hemodynamics. Maintaining adequate volume status with judicious crystalloid administration supports perfusion without volume overloading. All mandatory actions have been completed; this is the most clinically appropriate available action for ongoing supportive care.

At 95 minutes post-arrival, the door-to-balloon time target of <90 minutes has been exceeded. Although PCI has been arranged, fibrinolysis should be considered if PCI is still delayed, per AHA guidelines recommending fibrinolytic therapy when PCI cannot be performed within the recommended timeframe. This is a safety net measure to ensure timely reperfusion.

Patient has three-vessel CAD and diabetes with post-PCI status. While hemodynamics are currently stable (BP 125/75, MAP 92), crystalloid support may be indicated to maintain adequate preload and renal perfusion, particularly given contrast load from angiography and upcoming CABG planning. This is the only remaining available action and provides supportive care during the transition to surgical revascularization.
Post-PCI STEMI patient with three-vessel disease requiring CABG should be admitted to the CCU for intensive monitoring, hemodynamic surveillance, and surgical planning.
